title: Inner Product Spaces (6.1)
description: Day 35: inner product axioms, bilinearity, norm, distance, unit vectors, Theorem 6.1.1, weighted Euclidean, matrix-generated, M22 trace, P2, and C[a,b] inner products, impostors, and real vs. complex inner products. 10 questions pulled per attempt from a pool of 60.

questions.prompt: The axiom $\langle u,v\rangle = \langle v,u\rangle$ for a real inner product is called _____.
questions.explanation: Swapping the two inputs doesn't change a real inner product.

questions.prompt: The axiom $\langle u+v,w\rangle=\langle u,w\rangle+\langle v,w\rangle$ is called _____.
questions.explanation: The inner product distributes over vector addition in each slot.

questions.prompt: The axiom $\langle ku,v\rangle = k\langle u,v\rangle$ is called _____.
questions.explanation: Scalars pull out of the slot.

questions.prompt: The axiom “$\langle v,v\rangle\ge 0$, with equality only when $v=0$” is called _____.
questions.explanation: It is also called positive definiteness. It is what makes lengths meaningful.

questions.prompt: In any inner product space, the norm of $v$ is defined as $\|v\| =$ _____.
questions.explanation: The norm is the square root of the vector's inner product with itself.

questions.prompt: In an inner product space, the distance between $u$ and $v$ is $d(u,v)=$ _____.
questions.explanation: Distance is the norm of the difference.

questions.prompt: Because an inner product is linear in each slot separately, we say it is _____.
questions.explanation: Linear in the first slot plus symmetry gives linearity in the second slot too.

questions.prompt: For a complex inner product, symmetry is replaced by _____ symmetry: $\langle u,v\rangle=\overline{\langle v,u\rangle}$.
questions.explanation: Swapping the inputs conjugates the value.

questions.prompt: The standard inner product on $C[a,b]$ is $\langle f,g\rangle=$ _____.
questions.explanation: Multiply the functions and integrate. It is a continuous version of the dot product.

questions.prompt: In a real inner product space, $\langle u,v\rangle=\langle v,u\rangle$ for all $u,v$.
explanations: That is the symmetry axiom.

questions.prompt: In a real inner product space, $\langle u,kv\rangle = k\langle u,v\rangle$.
explanations: Use symmetry, pull the scalar out of the first slot, then use symmetry again.

questions.prompt: In any inner product space, $\langle 0,v\rangle = 0$ for every $v$.
explanations: $\langle 0,v\rangle=\langle 0\cdot 0,v\rangle = 0\langle 0,v\rangle=0$.

questions.prompt: In a real inner product space, $\langle u,v\rangle$ is always nonnegative.
explanations: Only $\langle v,v\rangle$ must be nonnegative. $\langle u,v\rangle$ itself can be negative. For example, $(1,0)\cdot(-1,0)=-1$.

questions.prompt: If $\langle v,v\rangle = 0$, then $v$ must be the zero vector.
explanations: That is part of the positivity axiom.

questions.prompt: $\|kv\| = k\|v\|$ for every scalar $k$.
explanations: It is $|k|\,\|v\|$. A norm can never be negative, so $k=-2$ gives $2\|v\|$, not $-2\|v\|$.

questions.prompt: $d(u,v)=d(v,u)$ in every inner product space.
Each vector space has exactly one inner product.
explanations: A space can have many: $\mathbb{R}^2$ has the dot product, every positive weighted product, every matrix-generated product, and more.

questions.prompt: The length of a vector depends on which inner product you use.
explanations: $(1,0)$ has length 1 under the dot product but length 2 under $\langle u,v\rangle=4u_1v_1+u_2v_2$.

questions.prompt: $\langle u+v,u+v\rangle = \langle u,u\rangle + \langle v,v\rangle$ in every inner product space.
explanations: Bilinearity gives $\langle u,u\rangle+2\langle u,v\rangle+\langle v,v\rangle$. The middle term vanishes only when $\langle u,v\rangle=0$.

questions.prompt: In a complex inner product space, $\langle u,v\rangle$ always equals $\langle v,u\rangle$.
explanations: They are complex conjugates: $\langle u,v\rangle=\overline{\langle v,u\rangle}$. They are equal only when the value is real.

questions.prompt: In a complex inner product space, $\langle v,v\rangle$ is always a real number.
explanations: By conjugate symmetry, $\langle v,v\rangle$ equals its own conjugate, so it is real. Positivity then makes it $\ge 0$.

questions.prompt: The unit “circle” $\{v:\|v\|=1\}$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$ is always a circle, whatever inner product you use.
explanations: For $3u_1v_1+2u_2v_2$ it is the ellipse $3x^2+2y^2=1$. Matrix-generated inner products give tilted ellipses.

questions.prompt: If $v\ne 0$, then $v/\|v\|$ is a unit vector.
explanations: By Theorem 6.1.1(b), $\|v/\|v\|\,\|=\frac{1}{\|v\|}\|v\|=1$, in any inner product.

explanations: Each weight must be strictly positive. A zero weight lets a nonzero vector have norm 0, and a negative weight gives a negative $\langle v,v\rangle$.

questions.prompt: With the weighted inner product $\langle u,v\rangle=3u_1v_1+2u_2v_2$, compute $\langle (1,-2),(4,1)\rangle$.
With $\langle u,v\rangle=3u_1v_1+2u_2v_2$, what is $\|(1,-2)\|^2$?
With $\langle u,v\rangle=4u_1v_1+u_2v_2$, what is $\|(1,0)\|$?
questions.explanation: $\sqrt{4\cdot1^2}=2$. The first axis is “stretched” by this inner product.

questions.prompt: With $\langle u,v\rangle=4u_1v_1+u_2v_2$, what is $\|(1,1)\|^2$?
In $M_{22}$ with $\langle U,V\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(U^TV)$, what is $\|I_2\|^2$?
questions.explanation: The entries are 1, 0, 0, 1, so $\|I_2\|^2=2$ and $\|I_2\|=\sqrt2$. The identity is not a unit vector.

questions.prompt: In $M_{22}$ with $\langle U,V\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(U^TV)$, compute $\left\langle \begin{bmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{bmatrix},\begin{bmatrix}-1&0\\3&2\end{bmatrix}\right\rangle$.
questions.explanation: Multiply matching entries: $-1+0+9+8=16$.

questions.prompt: In $C[0,1]$ with $\langle f,g\rangle=\int_0^1 f g\,dx$, compute $\langle x, x^2\rangle$. (Enter a fraction like 1/4.)
In $C[0,1]$ with $\langle f,g\rangle=\int_0^1 f g\,dx$, compute $\|x\|^2$.

In $C[-\pi,\pi]$ with $\langle f,g\rangle=\int_{-\pi}^{\pi} f g\,dx$, compute $\langle \sin x,\cos x\rangle$.
questions.explanation: $\sin x\cos x$ is an odd function, so its integral over a symmetric interval is 0.

questions.prompt: In $P_2$ with $\langle p,q\rangle=p(-1)q(-1)+p(0)q(0)+p(1)q(1)$, compute $\langle 1-x+x^2,\;2x+x^2\rangle$.
In $P_2$ with the coefficient inner product $\langle a_0+a_1x+a_2x^2,\,b_0+b_1x+b_2x^2\rangle=a_0b_0+a_1b_1+a_2b_2$, compute $\langle 1-x+x^2,\;2x+x^2\rangle$.
questions.explanation: $1\cdot0+(-1)(2)+1\cdot1=-1$. It is a different inner product from the evaluation one, so the answer differs.

questions.prompt: Given $\langle u,v\rangle=3$, $\|u\|=2$, $\|v\|=5$, compute $\|u+v\|^2$.
Given $\langle u,v\rangle=3$, $\|u\|=2$, $\|v\|=5$, compute $\langle 2u-v,\,u+3v\rangle$.
questions.explanation: $2\langle u,u\rangle+6\langle u,v\rangle-\langle v,u\rangle-3\langle v,v\rangle = 8+18-3-75=-52$.

questions.prompt: For the complex Euclidean inner product on $\mathbb{C}^2$, $u\cdot v=u_1\bar v_1+u_2\bar v_2$, compute $\|(i,1)\|^2$.
questions.explanation: $i\cdot\bar i + 1\cdot 1 = i(-i)+1 = 1+1=2$. Without the conjugate you would get $i^2+1=0$.

questions.prompt: Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\0&1\end{bmatrix}$ and $\langle u,v\rangle = Au\cdot Av$. Compute $\langle e_1,e_2\rangle$.
questions.explanation: $Ae_1=(1,0)$ and $Ae_2=(2,1)$, so the dot product is 2. The standard basis vectors are no longer “perpendicular.”
